correctness.rationale: For n>=m>=3, an empty row and empty column cannot coexist in a total dominating set. At optimum cardinality m, one orientation has exactly one selected square per column and each occupied row has at least two. Moves cannot change the orientation, column, or occupied-row support. A row with >=3 selections is a buffer enabling arbitrary exchanges among supports of size r>=2 and m>2r; when m=2r all rows have size two and every state is immobile. Fiber-surjection enumeration gives L_{m,r}=m![x^m](e^x-1-x)^r, and each directed move is counted by fixing an affected column, its source/destination labels and an admissible (m-1)-column remainder, yielding E_{m,r}=binom(r,2)*m*L_{m-1,r}. The m=5 component is the Desargues inclusion graph. Direct enumeration: full-board open-neighborhood and single-replacement graph; n,m=(3,3),(4,3),(4,4),(5,4),(5,5),(6,5); direct_output.txt. Independent associated-surjection enumeration m=3,...,8 and r<=floor(m/2), including vertex degrees, edges and components; structure_output.txt. Combinatorial proof: empty row/column forcing; frozen support; buffer-row transpositions; exponential generating counts; double-counted directed moves; 2/3-subset inclusion identification.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the full one-vertex-replacement graph decomposition of minimum total dominating sets, the exact mobility threshold and component size/edge formulas, and the five-column Desargues identification. Minimum cardinalities, counts, and component descriptions of inclusion-minimal (as opposed to minimum) total-dominating sets exist in related literature or earlier combinatorial records and are not presented as novel. Published 2013/2015 product-domination articles and 2020 reconfiguration survey were inspected at the relevant statements; no result stating or implying the exchange decomposition was found. A pre-existing paired-domination exchange result concerns a strict even-fiber subfamily, so does not imply the odd-fiber transitions. Search noncoverage is not a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A structurally equivalent token-jumping or surjection reconfiguration theorem could be unpublished or absent from the indexed/searchable literature.
Rook graph minimum-set counting and a broader minimal-total-domination classification are prior known; no novelty is attributed to their direct enumerative implications.

value.rationale: The minimum-solution exchange graph is the natural reachability structure for keeping an optimal total-dominating placement under one simultaneous replacement. The new all-board classification gives exact frozen-support obstructions, a constructive algorithm within every mobile component, exact associated-Stirling order and edge formulas, and a sharp change from entirely isolated optima for three or four columns to Desargues components for five. It explains why a complete count of optima alone misses severe disconnection and heterogeneous mobility, and supports exact optimal-placement sampling or local-search studies; no unrelated downstream theorem is assumed.
